quick_notes.title: Cell Theory
quick_notes.detail: All living things are made of cells. Proposed by Schleiden and Schwann. First observed by Robert Hooke (1665 - dead cell) and Leeuwenhoek (living cell).

quick_notes.title: Cell Organelles (The Nicknames)
quick_notes.detail: 1. Mitochondria : Powerhouse of the cell (produces ATP). 2. Lysosomes : Suicide bags (digestive enzymes). 3. Ribosomes : Protein factories. 4. Golgi Bodies : Packaging house. 5. Chloroplast : Kitchen of the cell (only in plants).

quick_notes.title: Nucleus
quick_notes.detail: Brain of the cell. Contains DNA and Chromosomes. Prokayotic (no nucleus - Bacteria), whereas Eukaryotic (nucleus present - Animals/Plants).

quick_notes.title: Plant vs Animal Cell
quick_notes.detail: Plant: Cell wall (Cellulose), large vacuole, Chloroplast. Animal : No cell wall, small vacuoles, Centrioles.

quick_notes.title: Tissues
quick_notes.detail: Group of similar cells. Animal : Epithelial, Connective (Blood/Bone), Muscular, Nervous. Plant : Meristematic (Growth) and Permanent (Xylem - Water, Phloem - Food).

lesson_intro: Today we study the 'Micro-World'. The Cell is the fundamental unit of life. In SSC, questions often focus on 'Cell Organelles' and their nicknames (e.g., Powerhouse, Suicide bag). We also explore Tissues—the groups of cells that perform specific functions. Toppers focus on 'Plant vs Animal cells'. Let's master the biology of the cell today.
